_comment: Source: Bellevue Traffic Video Dataset, City of Bellevue, Washington, USA.
Released by the City of Bellevue for research purposes. Footage captured
September 2017 from a pole-mounted traffic camera at 116th Ave NE / NE 12th St,
natively 1280x720. Provided 'as is' with no warranty (see dataset DISCLAIMER).
Both clips come from the SAME fixed camera, which is required: run_evaluation
applies one Config, hence one set of ROI polygons, to every video in this set.
Preprocessing: the source hourly recordings drop frames, so their container frame
rate is misleading (the 08:08 hour reports 27.6452 fps). The longest gap-free run
of each hour was measured at 33.33 ms +- 0.01 per frame, i.e. true 30 fps, and a
240 s window was cut from within that run and re-encoded at a constant 30 fps.
No frames were duplicated or interpolated. This matters because Waiting_Time
accumulates as dt = 1 / frame_rate and a variable rate would corrupt it.
Compass approach names are a labelling convention required by the config schema,
not true bearings. See config/bellevue_116th.json for the mapping to camera view.
